**Events are NAMED `event: change`, NOT default.** Use `es.addEventListener('change', handler)` - `es.onmessage` ONLY catches events WITHOUT an event: line, so it silently misses every framework broadcast. The js_snippet above wires both.
Don't open more than ONE EventSource per page - they accumulate connections.
Heartbeats are SSE comment lines (`: keepalive` every 25 s); EventSource never passes them to a handler. Keep the try/catch around JSON.parse for safety.
Events are scoped server-side: clients only receive mutations they're allowed to see (owner / org).

`/sse/events` returns 401 to anonymous clients when app.yaml has an `auth:` block (the default). A session or token whose account is held (MFA enrollment required, a temporary password to replace) gets that hold's 403 (`mfa_enrollment_required` / `password_change_required`) and no stream. EventSource carries the session cookie same-origin, so just being logged in is enough - no extra wiring. Set `features.ws_anonymous: true` to drop the gate for open-broadcast use cases. A development instance (a hosted `<sub>-dev` with `features.testing: true`) admits anonymous streams so the injected dev reload client works on pre-auth pages; they receive `event: reload` and, like any anonymous stream, the `change` events of tables whose read access is `anon` (those tables are public), and nothing for any other table. `/ws` has no such exception and answers an anonymous client 401 there. A prod instance with `features.testing` still on (promote does not turn it off; `benmore publish` does) answers anonymous clients 401 like any other prod instance. Signed-in tabs there still connect and reload.

Owner-scoped tables (and member-of, owner_or_role and declared self tables): only the writer and admins see the detailed `{table, action}` event; everyone else gets `{table:'', action:'refresh'}` (a refetch hint), so treat a refresh with an empty table as 'refetch what you show'. That includes a reader who sees someone else's row through a record share, in any tenant, since per-row grants are not resolved per event. Only tables with the `groups:` tenant key stay inside the writer's tenant; any other table reaches readers in every tenant.

Tables marked `access.read: anon` or `everyone` broadcast UNSCOPED - every connected viewer gets the named `{table, action}` event instead of the generic refresh (still no row data). Required for live-chat / public-feed patterns where every viewer needs to know about new rows the moment they're inserted.

SSE event payload is ALWAYS `{table, action}` - never the row itself. Clients re-fetch on each event. Canonical chat/feed pattern: keep a `lastId` cursor; on each event, `fetch('/api/messages?orderBy=id:asc&limit=200')`, append unseen rows.

**Flow writes notify too.** A flow's `run: sql` / `run: sql_dynamic` INSERT / REPLACE / UPDATE / DELETE (including steps nested under if / for_each / parallel / on_error, and cron, async and data-event flows) emits the same `{table, action}` event, once per table and action per run: after COMMIT for a `transaction: true` flow (a rollback emits nothing), and as each statement completes otherwise. Only schema tables are announced - never `_benmore_*` or full-text index tables - and a single-statement write that changed no rows is not announced. Delivery uses the same per-subscriber checks as auto-CRUD. Unlike auto-CRUD, a flow write fires no hooks.yaml entry and no `on: event` flow (api({at:'hooks'}) → triggers). A run without a signed-in session (cron, webhook, async job, data event, public flow) is scoped to the tenant or owner its trusted trigger data names, else only admins hear about a tenant table and other readers of an owner table get the generic refresh. A cron write reaches a tenant's members when it RETURNs the tenant column (`... RETURNING studio_id`). See api({at:'flows'}) → realtime_events.

Verify end-to-end from the CLI with `benmore probe <app> GET /api/_auth/profile --as <email> --keep-session` to mint a cookie, then `curl -N -H "Cookie: $COOKIE" /sse/events` to subscribe, then trigger a CRUD mutation as the same user.

A stream stays open while its client keeps reading, until the server's 30-minute rotation closes it (EventSource reconnects by itself). Each write has a deadline (30 s in the app, and on the hosted platform 60 s for any `text/event-stream` response): a client that stops reading is disconnected instead of holding the connection. A quiet stream is never cut for being idle before the rotation.

`features.sse: false` in app.yaml turns the endpoint off: `/sse/events` is not served (an EventSource request gets 404), so nothing that listens on it updates. It is on by default. `/ws` has its own switch, `features.ws`.
